items.headline: Amazon shares fall 6% as AI spending and slower e-commerce growth worry investors
items.summary: Amazon shares fall 6% as AI spending tops $77 billion in the quarter, e-commerce growth slows and free cash outflow reaches $42.4 billion.

items.headline: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
items.summary: Microsoft boasts a strong credit rating and has managed to maintain positive free cash flow, unlike Meta, Alphabet and Amazon.

items.headline: Intel stock plunges 21% as chipmaker blames PC slowdown for weak guidance
items.summary: Intel has been a Wall Street darling this year due to its emergence as a player in AI, but the company is being weighed down by a struggling PC market.

items.headline: Amazon AWS posts 39% revenue growth as cloud rivals also accelerate
items.summary: Amazon's cloud signed deals with Meta and OpenAI during the quarter, helping revenue to exceed consensus.

items.headline: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
items.summary: Reddit posts third-quarter earnings and reveals plans to require all users to create official accounts as Google search traffic shrinks

items.headline: Meta's $100 billion stock sale shrinks your slice of the company
items.summary: Meta’s AI buildout is outpacing its cash generation, prompting the ad giant to seek up to $100 billion from shareholders.

items.headline: Coinbase net income surges 66% in third quarter, benefiting from bitcoin investment gains
items.summary: Coinbase posted better-than-expected earnings in the third quarter, largely due to a recovery in the cryptocurrency market.

items.headline: Intel plunges on a major guidance miss. What went wrong — and how to proceed
items.summary: Further downside is certainly possible, but selling now won't erase the losses we've taken.

items.headline: How elections worldwide are testing Trump’s influence abroad
items.summary: Recent election losses by leaders linked to Trump have prompted questions about whether his influence over the global right is weakening.

items.headline: Intel shares plunge 21% as fourth-quarter revenue forecast misses estimates
items.summary: Intel shares plunge 21% after its fourth-quarter revenue forecast misses estimates, as weak PC demand and supply-chain issues weigh on its outlook.

items.headline: Binance 'potential security issue' sees $2.54 billion frozen by the likes of Circle, Tether
items.summary: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, said it was actively investigating the matter and that funds are "completley safe."

items.headline: DOJ escalates Alaska Senate lawsuit over dueling Sullivan candidacies
items.summary: Alaska's election could determine which party has a majority in the Senate. GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan faces a strong challenge from Democrat Mary Peltola.

items.headline: Amazon: Fear Is Back, But I'm Buying The Pullback (NASDAQ:AMZN)
items.summary: Amazon.com, Inc. earnings missed, but AWS growth, AI demand, and long-term upside stand out. Click for this AMZN update and see why I am bullish.

items.headline: Some Polymarket user funds stolen by hackers; exchange referring matter to U.K. authorities
items.summary: The outage comes just days before the platform is expected to experience heightened trading during the U.S. midterm elections.

items.headline: Amazon posts negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion, holds 2026 capex unchanged
items.summary: Amazon's negative free cash flow ballooned during the third quarter, while its earnings and revenue fell short of Wall Street's expectations.

items.headline: IRS CEO Bisignano donates to Trump Accounts in his childhood Brooklyn ZIP code
items.summary: IRS CEO Frank Bisignano has donated to Trump Accounts for Brooklyn kids from his hometown ZIP code. Here's what families need to know.

items.headline: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise
items.summary: Rivian also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.

items.headline: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam
items.summary: Starbucks' U.S. stores topped Wall Street's comparable sales expectations but its international business fell short of estimates.

items.headline: Alphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of search
items.summary: Wall Street hammered Alphabet for an earnings miss that included weaker-than-expected revenue out of the company's core business.

items.headline: Alphabet tanks nearly 13% for worst day ever, losing $500 billion in value
items.summary: Alphabet reported a larger negative free cash flow than analysts had expected while maintaining its spending gudiance for the year.
